The differing widths of the 90% confidence intervals directly reflect the increasing uncertainty associated with longer time horizons. Several specific risks or events could push the actual outcomes outside of these stated intervals. On the upside, an unanticipated major positive breakthrough, such as a significant technological innovation, a highly impactful new policy stimulus, or a sudden and widespread surge in economic confidence, could drive the value well above the upper bounds. These are typically low-probability, high-impact events that are difficult to foresee but possess the potential to significantly disrupt expected trajectories over any given horizon.
